--- title: "[Graph.get_edge_df_ws()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Get selected edges as a Polars DataFrame with standardized structure. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L7792-L7901){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.get_edge_df_ws() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Similar to `get_edge_df()` but only exports currently selected edges. Uses the same consistent column structure with `id`, `source`, `target`, and `rel` as first 4 columns. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [pl.DataFrame]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : DataFrame with edges sorted by id, containing: - column 1: `id` (i64, mandatory) - column 2: `source` (i64, mandatory) - column 3: `target` (i64, mandatory) - column 4: `rel` (str, mandatory, `None` if not set) - columns 5-N: Other attributes (alphabetically sorted) Returns empty DataFrame if no edges are selected. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} - first 4 columns always: `id`, `source`, `target`, `rel` (in that order) - missing rel values appear as `None` - DataFrame sorted by `id` ascending - same structure as `get_edge_df()` but filtered to selection ## Examples {.doc-examples} Selecting only the "friend" edges before exporting means the DataFrame contains just that subset: ::: {#621a58a0 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_node(label="D") .add_edge(source="A", target="B", weight=1.5, rel="friend") .add_edge(source="B", target="C", weight=0.5, rel="colleague") .add_edge(source="C", target="D", weight=2.0, rel="friend") .select_edges(lambda e: e.attributes and e.attributes.get("rel") == "friend") ) df = graph.get_edge_df_ws() df["rel"].value_counts() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: This makes it easy to run DataFrame analysis on just a subset of the graph's edges -- for example, the first few edges added: ::: {#43360395 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph().add_path_graph(10) edge_ids = list(graph.get_edge_ids())[:5] graph.select_edges_by_id(edge_ids) graph.get_edge_df_ws() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}
